0.long_answer: Livedoid vasculopathy is a rare disorder that primarily affects the small vessels of the skin, particularly those supplying the lower extremities. It is characterized by recurrent, painful ulcerations that eventually heal with porcelain-white atrophic scars, a feature that results in the term atrophie blanche. Historically, this condition was thought to be a subtype of small-vessel vasculitis; however, current evidence suggests that it is more accurately described as a thrombo-occlusive vasculopathy rather than a true inflammatory vasculitis. The pathogenesis involves thrombus formation within dermal vessels, contributing to the skin changes and ulcerations seen in affected patients.
